Binance US Moves Closer to U.S. Perpetual Futures as CFTC Clears DCM and DCO Applications for Substantive Review Binance US said the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has deemed its applications to register as a designated contract market (DCM) and derivatives clearing organization (DCO) substantially complete, moving them into substantive review. Neither application has been approved. DCM registration would allow Binance US to offer derivatives trading, including futures and options, while DCO registration would allow it to clear those trades. Binance US plans to use both registrations to offer U.S. users regulated derivatives, including perpetual futures. It has not launched any derivatives products and must await formal CFTC approval before doing so. According to the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) website, BAM Derivatives LLC submitted Binance US’s application to register as a designated contract market (DCM). The filing appeared in the public record on November 19 and is currently listed as “pending.” BAM Derivatives plans to list Bitcoin and Ether perpetual contracts, with BAM Clearing LLC providing clearing services. — link

Highlight Clip: Michael Saylor: Strategy Could Buy All Newly Mined Bitcoin in the Future Michael Saylor: Strategy Could Buy All Newly Mined Bitcoin in the Future On November 15, 2026, Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor said at the 2026 Cantor Convergence conference that the company could buy all newly mined Bitcoin between now and 2140, leaving other buyers to compete for the remaining supply and thereby driving prices higher. He likened Strategy to the central bank of the crypto economy, saying its Bitcoin holdings represented approximately 4.05% of the ultimate total supply and that it had raised nearly $22 billion this year despite the crypto winter. He argued that the company's value came not only from its roughly $65 billion to $70 billion in capital reserves, but also from its ability to create credit through instruments such as STRC. Creating more credit at a lower cost, he said, could make the company worth more than its underlying assets and generate greater returns for shareholders. — link

Spot Bitcoin ETFs See $582 Million in Net Outflows on November 19, Marking Third Consecutive Day On November 19 (ET), spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded total net outflows of $582 million, their third consecutive day of net outflows. Spot Ethereum ETFs recorded total net outflows of $131 million, marking their fifth consecutive day of net outflows. — link

Bloomberg: Coinbase Plans to Launch Its Own Prediction Market Contracts in the US in the First Half of 2027 Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Coinbase plans to launch its own prediction market event contracts for retail and institutional customers in the US in the first half of 2027. Coinbase currently offers prediction market services through a partnership with Kalshi. Launching its own contracts would give it greater control over product launches and allow it to retain more trading revenue. Coinbase announced its acquisition of prediction market startup The Clearing Company in December 2025 and received CFTC approval for its own clearinghouse in September 2026. In the third quarter of 2026, its prediction market business had an annualized revenue run rate exceeding $200 million. — link
